report:
## Conclusion: The claim is well-supported by evidence

The claim that the adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, brand name Shingrix) reduces shingles in adults aged 70 years or older is strongly supported by high-quality randomized controlled trial data and confirmed by long-term follow-up.

**Pivotal trial evidence:** The ZOE-70 trial (NCT01165229) was a placebo-controlled, observer-blind phase 3 trial specifically enrolling adults ≥70 years old, randomizing nearly 7,000 participants per arm to receive two doses of RZV or placebo. This trial, published in the *New England Journal of Medicine*, demonstrated significant efficacy against herpes zoster in this age group (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800). This built on the companion ZOE-50 trial in adults ≥50, which showed 97.2% efficacy (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1501184).

**Long-term durability:** A pooled long-term follow-up study (ZOE-LTFU) combining participants from ZOE-50 and ZOE-70 has tracked vaccine efficacy for up to 11 years post-vaccination. The final analysis, published in *eClinicalMedicine* (Lancet family journal), confirmed that RZV provides durable protection against herpes zoster and its complications across all age ranges ≥50 years, including those originally enrolled at 70+ (https://www.thelancet.com/journals/eclinm/article/PIIS2589-5370(25)00173-7/fulltext; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12235393/).

**Regulatory/public health endorsement:** Based on this trial evidence, the U.S. CDC recommends two doses of Shingrix for all immunocompetent adults aged 50 and older, a recommendation grounded in the ZOE-50/ZOE-70 efficacy data (https://www.cdc.gov/shingles/hcp/vaccine-considerations/index.html).

**Overall assessment:** Multiple independent, peer-reviewed randomized trials plus real-world long-term follow-up data converge to support this claim. The evidence quality is high (large RCTs, peer-reviewed, replicated over 11 years), making this a well-substantiated health claim.
